ops_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to create our company's Google Workspace account (Gmail, Calendar, Docs suite). This requires an authorized officer's approval before Google's subscription/billing terms are accepted, so you must stop short of submitting the signup.

First, ask me for any of the following if not already provided:
- Our company's legal/business name
- The primary domain we want to use for company email (or whether we still need to purchase one)
- Estimated number of employees/users who will need accounts
- Preferred billing contact name and email
- Preferred Workspace plan tier (e.g., Business Starter, Standard, Plus) if I have a preference, or ask me to note this is a decision the approver should make

Then do the following:
1. Go to https://workspace.google.com/ and review the current signup flow, plan options, and pricing tiers so you can summarize them for me.
2. Draft a concise summary document covering: company name, domain to use, number of users, recommended plan tier with pricing, and any admin setup notes (e.g., admin email address to use, DNS verification requirement for the domain).
3. Prepare a checklist of every field the signup form will ask for, pre-filled with the information I gave you, so the approver can complete the form quickly.
4. Note explicitly that clicking submit and accepting Google's Terms of Service/billing agreement commits the company to a paid subscription, and that this action must be taken by an authorized signatory using their own credentials.

Do not fill out or submit the actual signup form, and do not accept any terms of service on my behalf. Once the summary and checklist are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the completed summary document, the pre-filled checklist, the recommended plan and pricing, and a clear statement that the account creation and terms acceptance remain a human step.

ops_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me verify domain ownership for Google Workspace so I can finish setting up company email, calendar, and docs. Before starting, ask me for: (1) my company domain name, (2) confirmation that I have already created (or want you to create) a Google Workspace account for this domain, (3) which domain registrar or DNS host manages this domain (e.g., GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudflare, Google Domains, etc.), and (4) confirmation that you should use my configured credentials to access both the Google admin console and the DNS host's dashboard.

Once you have these details:
1. Log into the Google admin console using my configured credentials and navigate to the domain verification section for Workspace.
2. Retrieve the verification record Google provides — this will be either a TXT record or a CNAME record with a specific host and value.
3. Log into the DNS host's dashboard using my configured credentials and add that exact TXT or CNAME record to the domain's DNS settings, matching the host, type, and value Google specified.
4. Save the DNS change, then return to the Google admin console and trigger the verification check.
5. If verification fails due to DNS propagation delay, wait and retry rather than making further changes; report if it fails after a reasonable retry period (e.g., a few hours) since DNS propagation timing remains a human step to monitor.

Done looks like: the Google admin console confirms the domain is verified and Workspace status shows ownership confirmed.

Report back with: the domain verified, the exact DNS record type/host/value you added, confirmation of successful verification (or details of any failure/error message), and any next steps Google's console indicates (e.g., setting up MX records) that I should know about.

ops_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up user accounts in {{vendor}}, our company email/calendar/docs suite, as part of onboarding our team. Before doing anything, ask me for: (1) my company domain, (2) the list of team members to create accounts for (full name, desired username/email alias, department or role, and whether they need admin privileges), and (3) confirmation that our {{vendor}} admin console access is already configured with your credentials.

Once you have this information, prepare a complete account creation plan: for each team member, draft the proposed email address, display name, job title/department, and account type (standard user vs. admin). Check the plan for naming consistency (e.g., firstname.lastname@domain) and flag any duplicate usernames or missing information. Do not create or modify any accounts yet.

Present me with a clear summary table of all proposed accounts, including any flagged issues or open questions, and clearly state the exact settings that will be applied (aliases, admin roles, groups if mentioned). Because this step requires a human to explicitly approve changes before they are applied, you must stop for human sign-off after presenting the plan — do not create, activate, or provision any accounts until I confirm approval.

After I approve, proceed to create the approved accounts in {{vendor}}'s admin console using your configured credentials, following the confirmed details exactly. Report back with a final list of accounts created, their status (active/pending), and any errors or accounts that could not be created, along with next steps for resolving them.

ops_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the setup of shared drives in Google Drive as part of our Google Workspace configuration. This step requires my explicit approval before any shared drive is actually created, so your job is to prepare a complete, ready-to-execute plan and then stop.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) our company domain, (2) the list of shared drives we need (e.g. by department or team — Engineering, Marketing, Finance, etc.), (3) for each drive, who should be a member and at what access level (Manager, Content Manager, Contributor, Commenter, Viewer), and (4) any naming convention or folder structure preferences.

Using that information, produce a clear draft plan listing: each shared drive's proposed name, its purpose, the members to add with their exact permission levels, and any initial top-level folder structure within it. Check our existing Google Workspace setup (using my configured credentials) to confirm there are no naming conflicts with existing shared drives, and note any groups or users that don't yet exist so I can address them first.

Compile this into a single, well-organized summary (a table or numbered list is fine) that I can review at a glance, showing exactly what will be created and who will have access to what. Do not create, modify, or apply any changes to Google Drive — do not create the shared drives, add members, or set permissions yet.

When the plan is ready, present it to me and stop for human sign-off. Report back with the full draft plan, any conflicts or missing prerequisites you found, and a clear statement that no changes have been applied pending my approval.

ops_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the security configuration for our company's {{vendor}} email, calendar, and docs suite (admin console). This is part of setting up company email & docs. Before doing anything, ask me for: (1) our company domain, (2) the list of team members/admins who need accounts, (3) any specific security requirements I already have (e.g., mandatory 2-factor authentication, password strength/rotation rules, session length limits, third-party app access restrictions, or device management policies).

Using your configured credentials, sign in to the {{vendor}} admin console and review the current security settings, including: two-factor authentication (2FA) enforcement status, password policy, login challenge/session settings, and any third-party app or API access controls. Draft a clear, concrete security configuration plan that includes: recommended 2FA enforcement (e.g., required for all users), password policy settings, session/login security rules, and any recommended restrictions on third-party app access — tailored to a small team unless I specify otherwise.

Do NOT apply, save, or submit any changes in the admin console. Your job is only to prepare a checklist/plan showing exactly which settings you recommend, their current values, and their proposed new values, along with a brief rationale for each. Present this plan to me in a clear list format for review.

Once the plan is ready, stop for human sign-off — do not enable, toggle, or confirm any settings yourself. Report back with the full checklist of proposed security settings and clearly state that you are awaiting my explicit approval before any changes are applied.
